prize_parts.citation: For the development of base editors that chemically convert single DNA bases in living cells, programmably and without double-strand breaks

statement.case_for: I keep base editing as my preferred configuration and I have not changed it from round 1. After reading all eight statements, it is the only candidacy where three members independently converged on the same three names and nearly the same citation, and I weigh that as agreement about the science and not as a vote count. The structural and mechanistic evidence is what persuades me. A deaminase is tethered to a Cas9 nickase so that one base within a narrow window is chemically converted, and the products are verified at nucleotide resolution in cells. The adenine editor needed a TadA deaminase evolved to act on DNA, an activity that has no natural counterpart, which is new chemistry and not a repackaging of an existing tool. Many independent laboratories have reproduced and extended both editor families, and first clinical use exists. Credit follows the sequence of the work: the concept and cytosine editor from Komor and Liu, the adenine editor from Gaudelli and Liu.
statement.case_against: The honest weaknesses remain the increment over the 2020 prize and the youth of the field (2016-2017). The 2020 citation was about guided double-strand cleavage, and a committee could still read base editing as an engineering extension of that platform. Kondo and Nishida's Target-AID cytidine deaminase fusion is an independent and near-simultaneous result that the three-name limit leaves out, and I cannot claim that exclusion is free of cost. Off-target deamination, bystander editing and delivery are not settled, and the clinical record is short. If the committee judges that two decades of confirmation are needed, then B068 or the mature B008 are stronger on maturity, and I would accept that argument.

responses.point: Base editing is the one shortlisted candidacy that is a clearly attributable invention with a stated chemical mechanism, and the Liu, Komor, Gaudelli trio follows the actual sequence of the work.
responses.response: I agree on the mechanism and the attribution logic, and I take your asking for the citation to carry the chemistry as the right condition. I have therefore written deamination of single bases in living cells, without double-strand breaks, into my citation so it cannot be read as a second genome-cleavage prize. Where I am more cautious is your point about breadth of support. Somfai, Sparr and Aqvist place B006 low, so I would not call the case shared by the whole committee. It has to stand on the evidence, and I think it does.

responses.point: Base editing is a defined chemical reaction under programmable control, the adenine editor required directed evolution of TadA, and the 2020 prize honoured cleavage and not base conversion.
responses.response: Your argument answers the chair's first question well. The 2020 prize concerned the guided nuclease, while base editing is a distinct reaction in which the cell's own repair converts a deamination intermediate into a stable base change. I do share your worry about the maturity record. Long-term off-target deamination and bystander editing are still open, and I would not call it settled. I differ with you slightly on Target-AID. You treat the exclusion as something a careful reader could call unfair, and I agree. Because of the three-person cap I still cannot see a cleaner cut than Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, since neither Kondo nor Nishida developed the adenine editor or the clinical line.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation (B068) is a genuine molecular design principle with clinical-stage degraders and an approved cereblon glue lineage, and the 2020 prize is a stronger obstacle for base editing than others admit.
responses.response: I agree that B068 is the most credible other configuration, and it remains my first alternative. The 2020 obstacle I do not accept as decisive. Cleavage and base conversion are different chemical events, whereas the heterobifunctional PROTAC and the cereblon glue are two separable discoveries that a three-name prize must split between Crews and Deshaies on one side and Handa on the other. That leaves Ciulli's ternary-complex structural work, which I value as a structural chemist, outside the prize. The missing approved heterobifunctional degrader is for me a real maturity gap that base editing, with first clinical use, has begun to close.

responses.point: Phase separation is the one candidate that is a new organizing principle and physical chemistry in the strict sense, and the link between theory and measurement is the standard for a prize.
responses.response: I respect the standard of quantitative testability, and base editing meets it in a different way, since editing windows, efficiencies and products are directly measurable at nucleotide resolution. My difficulty with B056 is structural evidence. Which cellular assemblies are liquids in vivo is still contested, and a prize would rest partly on reconstitution experiments that do not yet map cleanly onto cell function. Pappu and Mittag would also be left out, which you concede. I would reconsider if the committee judged that the in vitro physical-chemical framework is mature enough by itself, but I do not think the in vivo question is merely a normal open issue.

responses.point: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B032) is the clearest general synthetic method on the shortlist, mature, with clean two-person attribution.
responses.response: I accept that B032 is the most mature and the cleanest attribution on the table, and a synthetic method with this record deserves a serious hearing. I still read it as an increment on the 2010 cross-coupling prize, with the Kosugi tin-amide precedent adding a priority question. I put that overlap above the CRISPR proximity, because the 2010 citation covered the Pd cross-coupling concept itself. If the committee prefers a mechanism-based, mature configuration, I would rank B032 above B056 and B048, but I do not move it above base editing.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that deamination without cleavage is a sufficiently distinct chemical achievement from the 2020 prize, and whether the citation wording is enough to make that clear.
Whether leaving out Kondo and Nishida can be defended on the grounds of the three-person limit and the adenine editor and clinical lineage, or whether Liu alone would be a more defensible prize.
Whether the short clinical record and unsettled off-target and bystander questions make 2026 premature, in which case the more mature B068 or B008 would be stronger.
Whether the committee will converge on any configuration, since round 1 shows one plurality of three and no majority.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. No member disclosed a specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, which is a connection among committee members and not to any candidate, and I have no apparent personal or institutional tie to Liu, Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo, Nishida or the other shortlisted names. I request no recusal.
